headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.38 (95% CI: 1.02–1.85), suggesting that ultra-processed food intake is associated with a higher risk of renal cell carcinoma. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

design.excerpt: In the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study, a US prospective cohort

effect_size.excerpt: Higher UPF intake was associated with higher RCC [HR (95% CI)<sub>Q4 vs Q1</sub> = 1.16 (1.05-1.29), p-trend = 0.0006] and cc-RCC risk [1.38 (1.17-1.62), p-trend <0.0001].
